theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBandRawARow.meets {pMain pCopy pFill : ℕ}
    (hmain : P[pMain]?=some (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBandRawARow.body pCopy pFill))
    (hcopy : P[pCopy]?=some _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.copyBody) (hfill : P[pFill]?=some _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.fillBody)
    (hw : (lim.space : ℤ) ≤ lim.word) (hd : d < lim.depth)
    (hsrc : src+n ≤ values) (hvalues : values+n ≤ owners)
    (howners : owners+n ≤ positions) (hspace : positions+n ≤ lim.space)
    (hstart : start+n ≤ lim.space) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Meets lim P pMain d [src,values,owners,positions,n,owner,start] μ (_root_.ThreeSum.LightBandRawARow.time n)
      (fun _ ν =>
        (∀ j < n, ν (values+j)=μ (src+j) ∧
          ν (owners+j)=(owner : ℤ) ∧ ν (positions+j)=((start+j : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
        _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBandRawARow.KeptOthers μ ν values owners positions n) := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Assume copy and fill helpers and the row body are installed. A length-$n$ source precedes ordered value, owner, and position arrays; all extents and the original start plus $n$ fit memory, and addresses fit words. With one call level available, the procedure copies every source value and writes the constant owner and successive original positions, changing only those three output windows within the row-time bound.

This row contract retains physical input indices even when several original integers have equal values.
